text:
alice: heads up — CI is red on my feature/serializer-refactor branch after yesterday's push. shard 4 times out in TestSerialization::test_large_object_serialization. can someone take a look? :cry:

ci-bot: CI Reporter — build 21456 failed on shard 4. failing test: tests/serialization/test_serializer.py::TestSerialization::test_large_object_serialization

ben: i'll grab the shard logs and rerun the shard now. ping me if it's urgent.

ci-bot: Re-run requested by ben — queued (shard=4)

carla: quick note — i can repro something similar locally when i run the whole file, but single test passes for me. might be a resource/parallelism timing issue.

alice: interesting — single test passes locally for me too. the failure shows an "AssertionError: timed out after 120s" in the test harness.

ben: log snippet from CI (shard 4):
```
E   AssertionError: timed out after 120s
../tests/serialization/test_serializer.py:87: AssertionError
Thread dump: waiting on serializer.flush()
Last seen: processed 2.4M objects, 120s wall
```

dmitri: that "waiting on serializer.flush()" smells like our new chunked-writes change. i pushed chunking earlier in the refactor — maybe a deadlock when buffer hits certain size.

carla: @dmitri could it be the new flush-on-close race? i saw a flaky on CI a while back but assumed infra.

dmitri: possible. i'll try running stress locally: `pytest tests/serialization/test_serializer.py::TestSerialization::test_large_object_serialization -k large_object -q --maxfail=1` in a loop.

alice: ben — any luck with rerun?

ben: rerun finished — still failing on shard 4, same timeout. attaching full shard log to the ticket.

ben: i tried reproducing with `tox -e py` on my laptop with 8 workers, still green. maybe the CI container is memory constrained and causes flush to block.

carla: can we increase the test timeout as a short-term mitigation? if it's an infra pressure issue that might buy time while we bisect.

dmitri: i prefer bisecting first — if a recent commit in this branch regressed, we should find it. alice, do you know the point where this started?

alice: it started after i merged main yesterday around commit `a1b2c3d` — i merged main then pushed. suspect commit in this branch: `f5e6d7c` (serializer: chunking + flush change)

ben: if nobody objects i'll kick off a local git bisect between `a1b2c3d` and HEAD. takes ~30min on my machine but will give us the culprit.

carla: +1 do the bisect. also can someone try repro in a container with limited memory (1.5GB) to mimic CI? i can set that up.

ci-bot: Note: rerun count = 1 for build 21456. please open a ticket if this persists.

ben: starting `git bisect start; git bisect good a1b2c3d; git bisect bad HEAD` now. will update with the first bad commit.

alice: thanks ben. if bisect points to dmitri's change, @dmitri can you review for a potential deadlock in flush()? if it's infra we'll revert the chunking change for now.

carla: local container repro (1.5GB) reproduces the wait consistently. i'll post the docker command in the ticket.

ben: bisect update — found first bad commit `f5e6d7c` (author dmitri). marking it here, please verify @dmitri.

dmitri: ack — i'll revert the change and push a minimal fix to avoid the blocking flush under constrained memory. thanks for bisecting so fast.

alice: once there's a patch can someone run the flaky test suite on CI with a couple reruns? i'll hold off merging until green.

ben: noted. once dmitri's patch is up i'll run the flaky job (3 reruns) to confirm.

dmitri: pushing fix now. small change: ensure flush runs with non-blocking fallback when buffer is full. will link PR.

alice: awesome — thanks team! :rocket:

ci-bot: Build 21489 (PR #987) triggered by dmitri — running shard 4.

ben: watching the CI — if it stays green i'll merge the fix and re-run your branch, alice.

carla: also adding a small integration test harness that runs the serializer under low-memory docker to catch this in CI going forward.

alice: perfect. i'll rebase once fix is merged and report back if anything else crops up. cheers.
